content_of_post_to_answer: How do trauma and mental health issues contribute to regret in later years, and what can be done about it early on?
answer: Trauma can make regret feel like a verdict when it was often a survival strategy at the time. People may later grieve choices they couldn't safely make, relationships they couldn't sustain, or years spent coping rather than living. Early help matters because it can create enough safety to separate "what happened to me" from "who I became." I've explored this pattern more deeply on my profile if you want to go further. Regret becomes more useful when it stops being a courtroom and becomes information.
